text:
incident-bot: AUTOPAGER triggered: gpu-node-72 is NotReady (kubelet unresponsive) + serial console silent. PagerDuty alert: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD-98765 - paging oncall. Severity: P1.

alice_oncall: acked. I'm taking primary.

ben_ops: I'm up next. ping me if you need hw access.

carla_infra: attaching serial now, trying to get kernel logs. initial console shows a hard CPU error then silence.

carla_infra: paste: ```
[ firmware ] PCI: can't find BAR for device 0000:3b:00.0
[ 1023.456789] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 00000000
[ 1023.456800] RIP: 0010:do_divide_error+0x14/0x20
[ 1023.456810] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
```

ben_ops: confirmed via dmesg over serial. This looks like a kernel oops -> panic. Could be NVMe/GPU firmware or motherboard.

alice_oncall: checking cluster impact: running quick query on pods scheduled to node.

alice_oncall: ```
$ kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-72
NAMESPACE   NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE         IP
ml-prod     model-server-xyz-0            0/1     Pending   0          3h    gpu-node-72  10.32.5.72
infra       metric-exporter-5b6d7        0/1     CrashLoop  3          2d    gpu-node-72  10.32.5.72
```

devex_kai: noticed ~4% spike in 503s to model-serving for a handful of high-traffic tenants starting ~2m ago. Likely these pods were on that node. I'm opening a quick customer-impact thread.

ben_ops: I'll attempt IPMI soft power-cycle while infra collects logs. Starting: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-72 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle`

carla_infra: running `nvme-cli` and smart logs from BMC when it comes back. If soft cycle fails, we'll escalate to host RMA.

alice_oncall: cordoning the node to avoid scheduling once it returns.

alice_oncall: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-72
node/gpu-node-72 cordoned
```

ben_ops: IPMI reports node powered off -> coming back up. Serial shows grub then immediate kernel panic again.

carla_infra: repeated kernel panic during boot. Dumping kernel oops/panic logs to S3: s3://redwood-ops/err/gpu-node-72/6543210000/panic.log

alice_oncall: draining any remaining pods (force) to reduce customer disruption, migrating critical pods to other nodes.

alice_oncall: ```
kubectl drain gpu-node-72 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```

devex_kai: rerouting traffic for affected tenants to fallback instances. I'll post updates to the customer-impact thread.

ben_ops: hardware team looped in. Ticket created: RMA-6421. Preliminary: suspected GPU PCIe fault causing system interrupt storm -> kernel panic.

carla_infra: while we wait for physical RMA, marking node unschedulable and removing from LB pools. Verified pods relocated.

alice_oncall: TL;DR customer impact: brief failures for ~5 tenants, transient 503s, automatic retries handled most, a small subset saw degraded latency for ~3 minutes. Escalating to SRE for postmortem if RMA needed.

ben_ops: handoff to infra for RMA/repair. I'll stay on-call for HW verification.

alice_oncall: handing over. @carla_infra take ownership for the repair ticket and follow the host-failure runbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbooks/host-kernel-panic. Noted steps: collect serial logs, IPMI logs, nvme smartctl, schedule on-site RMA.

carla_infra: acknowledged. Creating JIRA INC-6543 with attached logs and outage window. Notifying on-call hardware team.

pagerduty-bot: Alert closed by alice_oncall. PagerDuty incident PD-98765 assigned to carla_infra for RMA follow-up.

alice_oncall: marking thread resolved in slack, keep monitoring cluster alerts for repeat panics. If recurrence within 24h, escalate to platform lead. :white_check_mark:

ben_ops: leaving a short snippet for postmortem: possible PCIe topology glitch -> triggers divide error in do_divide_error path (weird), collect kernel module versions and firmware dumps.

carla_infra: attaching kernel version and lscpu output to the ticket.

devex_kai: posting customer impact summary to the customer-facing status page now.

alice_oncall: final note: no broad cluster impact, mitigations worked (drain + reroute). Follow-up: RMA and firmware validation scheduled. Thanks all. :heart:
